transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-11
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~42 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tomas (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO, Aurorix), Jake (Lead ML Eng), Alex (DevOps), Rina (Product)

--- Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Aurorix wants to evaluate Redwood for a production summarization pipeline and internal semantic search. Primary constraints: PII, EU data residency for some customers, and sub-200ms 95p latency on short requests. They prefer a PLG/self-serve path if TTFT is fast, otherwise will consider private/VPC.

00:00 Priya: Hey all, thanks for doing this, we wanted to run through how fast we can get to first call and what the options are.
00:12 Maya (Redwood AE): Yeah for sure, appreciate you folks. So quick agenda — confirm use case, understand constraints, talk hosted quickstart and credits, and then Tomas will do a high-level on private/VPC stuff if it looks necessary.
00:28 Jake: Use case — low-latency summarization of user documents and embeddings for search. Mix of short queries (20-150 tokens) and longer generation (up to 1k tokens) for batched jobs. We need to understand cost profile for both.
00:45 Tomas (SE): Cool. A couple clarifying q's, do you expect real-time per-request strict SLAs or more eventual batch throughput? Also where is your infra — mostly US, some EU customers?
01:02 Priya: Real-time for the UI — 95th perc under 200ms is ideal for short prompts. EU residency for certain clients is required, so any hosted option needs either regional hosting in eu-west or we look at private deploy.
01:18 Alex (DevOps): Also we have strict KMS policies; keys need to be customer-controlled if possible.
01:27 Maya: Great, that makes sense. Our PLG quickstart tends to be the fastest path to TTFT — usually minutes to a first token with our hosted API and SDK with sample app. We also provide free trial credits to validate cost and latency.
01:42 Rina: How many credits are typical? And are there gotchas?
01:48 Maya: We usually give a 30-day credit pack sized to run basic workloads — sample is 50k tokens worth but we can tailor. The main gotcha is that with hosted you accept our platform controls and our default retention policies; for strict KMS/customer-managed keys, the Private option is recommended.
02:10 Jake: If we tried hosted, how long to set up the quickstart? We have engineers available but want something low-friction.
02:18 Maya: If you go self-serve you can sign up, install the SDK in a dev environment and call the API in a few hours; for production-grade you'll want to configure rate limits, and maybe pin a model — that's a day or two.
02:33 Tomas: For the latency target, on hosted we typically route to region-specific clusters. For short prompts on a small model or an accelerated variant, 95p under 200ms is often doable but depends on queuing and batch config. We can run a small benchmark with your sample payload to give a real number.
02:55 Priya: Right, we care about tails. Do you do KV cache or prefix caching? We have a lot of repeated context for customers.
03:03 Tomas: Yes — runtime supports prefix/K V cache — sorry you might see that as K V cash in some logs — it helps reduce redundant compute. We also have intelligent batching which groups similar requests.
03:18 Alex: About private: what changes operationally? Does Redwood still manage the control plane?
03:25 Tomas: For Private we offer two modes: VPC-connected private with Redwood control plane but customer VPC peering, and fully on-prem where you run the inference nodes and we provide orchestration. Control-plane visibility and audit logs are available; for on-prem HSM or customer KMS you can keep keys local.
03:45 Priya: That sounds promising. Biggest blockers are SOC2 evidence, SSO with our IdP (SAML), and a clear audit trail.
03:53 Maya: We can share SOC2 report, SAML SSO guide, and a network diagram template. I'll send those after the call.
04:02 Rina: Another practical question — our product folks want to know how to charge back cost to customers. Does Redwood give per-route token breakdowns?
04:10 Tomas: Yes, Console will give token-level billing, per-route and per-model. There's also token latency histograms. We can export CSVs for internal chargeback.
04:22 Jake: Cost-wise, how does hosted compare to buying reserved capacity? We're projecting tens of millions of tokens per month in steady-state in 3–6 months.
04:30 Maya: Short answer: hosted is pay-as-you-go, good for prototyping and PLG. Dedicated/reserved capacity gives better predictable unit economics at scale and lower tail latency due to isolation. We can model this for your workload once you send sample traffic patterns.
04:50 Priya: Any notes on model variants or quantization? We plan to run some lighter quantized models for search and larger for long-form gen.
04:57 Tomas: We support quantized variants and can recommend profiles — e.g., 4-bit for embeddings workloads is common. For large gen you might choose a higher-accuracy variant. We'll share recommendations after the benchmark.
05:12 Alex: Network details — for VPC peering, what ports and CIDRs? We're on a tight firewall policy.
05:19 Tomas: We'll send a specific network checklist; in general we use standard HTTPS/443 for control plane and secure gRPC for data in some configs; private peering needs a couple CIDR ranges and NAT rules.
05:32 Priya: Ok, timeline — if we wanted to do a hosted quickstart first and then move to private in 6 weeks, is that supported?
05:40 Maya: Yes that's a common path — PLG first, then Dedicated or Private when you need residency or keys. We have a migration playbook. The trick is to pin model versions and plan for rollouts so users don't see regressions.
05:55 Rina: Who from Redwood would own the pilot?
06:00 Maya: I'll own the commercial side and Tomas will lead the SE work for the pilot and deep-dive. Likely a two-week pilot with trial credits and a performance benchmark.
06:10 Jake: For the benchmark, we'll provide a 1k-token payload set and a stream of 200 QPS? Our peak is about 150 QPS now but we want headroom.
06:22 Tomas: That sounds fine. We'll run a configured benchmark against hosted and a simulated private variant. Note that the private numbers may vary based on instance types and NICs.
06:35 Priya: One more — data deletion and retention. Can we set shorter retention for logs and payloads?
06:41 Maya: Yes, for Private you can control retention; for hosted we offer configurable retention windows and data deletion on request, but for stricter compliance we usually recommend Private. We'll include the retention options in the security doc.
06:55 Alex: Any integration with our existing observability stack? We use Datadog and internal tracing.
07:02 Tomas: Console exposes tracing hooks and you can send spans to your tracing backend; metric exports for Datadog via agent are supported. We'll include an integration note.
07:18 Priya: Are there any hard blockers that customers usually see in the onboarding?
07:24 Maya: Most blockers are around SSO and network approvals. Also some customers need a legal review for data residency. Those are solvable but take time — hence the suggestion of starting with hosted quickstart for TTFT and then parallel legal/security work for Private.
07:40 Jake: Ok, that seems workable.
07:46 Maya: Quick recap — next steps: we'll send SOC2 + SAML docs, PRD for private checklist, grant trial credits, and schedule SE deep-dive next Wednesday 11am PT. You'll send sample payloads and QPS numbers. Anything else?
07:58 Priya: Please put the pricing sheet with reserved capacity numbers — we want a sense of committed discounts vs paygo.
08:04 Maya: Yes will include pricing sheet.
08:08 Rina: Also can you share an example of the quickstart repo and a small sample app for embedding + search?
08:13 Tomas: We'll dm repo link and a small sample with Node and Python.
08:19 Priya: Thanks, this is great.
08:22 Maya: Appreciate the time, we'll follow up with the docs and links by Tuesday.

--- End meeting transcript (timestamps are approximate).

Notes on transcription noise: occasional speaker attributions may be off; some technical terms transcribed imperfectly ("K V cash" for KV cache, "control plane" sometimes "control plain").

Recap (single-line): Aurorix will trial Redwood hosted quickstart to validate TTFT and latency with trial credits; concurrently Redwood will provide security and network docs to scope a private/VPC pilot to meet KMS and EU residency requirements.
